body:
P2-12 PLAN 6/6: FIXTURES, VERSIONS, CACHE DETAILS (the list of tests by name is in the P2-12 section; a test never makes a real request)
GUARD FIRST: an autouse fixture in server/encore_server/tests/conftest.py makes any socket connect raise except to loopback and to the host of IT_NAVIDROME_URL (tests/integration are marked integration and excluded by default; they reach their pinned music server through that variable, so a blanket non-loopback block would break them), so no test, old or new, can reach Deezer by mistake (it also protects the cover finder's tests). FIXTURES: app/test/fixtures/deezer/search.json (20 real searches recorded 22 Oct 2026: artist, album and track each) MOVES to a shared path read by both suites, it is not copied; the App and the Server workflow both list that path in their filters, or a change to it runs only one side (docs/30 section I). The other shapes (artist, top, albums, album, album tracks, chart) have no recording in the repository (deezer_client_test.dart's are hand-written): they are built from the documented Deezer shape plus the fields the mappers read and named "synthetic" until the lead runs tools/record_catalogue_fixtures.py ONCE (at most 10 paced requests, one per shape and one namesake artist, from a development machine and not a Host's address; trimmed to the fields the mappers read, scrubbed). The server's own test WRITES the answers of its routes as app/test/fixtures/server/catalogue-*.json (ENCORE_WRITE_FIXTURES=1, the pattern of library-files-with-merges.json, ADR-R41 T5) and the app's parser must read them, so a change of the answer fails the server's CI first.
WHAT THE TESTS DO NOT PROVE: Deezer's real limits, and latency on a phone. Both are measured in the walk with the app's [perf] spans before (phone to Deezer) and after (phone to server to Deezer) on VM 108 and the A35: p50 and the worst of N, setup written beside the number (docs/30 section E). Nothing is marked walked.
VERSIONS, four pairings (an app never tries a route to find out): old app + new server: the app keeps calling Deezer itself, nothing breaks; new app + new server: the feature is listed, the app asks the server; new app + an Encore server without the feature (not updated, or the Host's switch is off): no catalogue sections, no request to Deezer, the P1-16 line in Search says what is missing, nothing greyed or nagging (ADR-R42 point 8); new app + a plain music server: the old path until slice 7, then no catalogue (D1). info.features is read once per session and on the live channel's resync; a 503 source_busy is the live signal. Timeouts: 2.0 s per outside request (1.0 s connect), 2.5 s per call, no retry (docs/17 section 7: search 3 s), so the server answers before the phone's own 4 s limit for these calls (the phone's Dio is 6/30/30 s, B-74).
CACHE DETAILS: the unit is the outside request, so a composite answer is assembled from cached parts and single flight works per part; one SQLite file catalogue-cache.db (WAL) in the data folder: not in the backup (backup.py copies encore.db and the music server's database only), deletable at any time, its writes never contend with the library's; key = sha256 of kind, path and sorted parameters (no typed text readable, no person id, no query in the info log); body = the outside JSON trimmed to the fields the mappers read, mapped on read, so a change of our shape never voids the cache; stale on error up to 30 days; at most 20,000 entries or 50 MB, the oldest deleted at start and every 1,000 inserts. Time to live: search 15 min, artist 24 h, artist top 24 h, releases 6 h, album and album tracks 7 days, chart 6 h, a valid empty answer 5 min. A release Deezer lists late is Deezer's lag (F12), not the cache's: the longest a listed release waits behind the cache is 6 hours.
